title: Salvianolic acid B attenuates abdominal aortic aneurysm via inhibition of ferroptosis and inflammation.
authors: Jin, Si-Jia; Dou, En-Guang; Wang, Lei; Qi, Lian-Wen; Wei, Feng; Zhang, Lei
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹酚酸B通过抑制铁死亡和炎症治疗腹主动脉瘤，核心为疾病药理机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall degeneration, inflammation, and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) loss. Despite extensive research, no effective pharmacological treatment is currently available to prevent or halt AAA progression. PURPOSE: This study aimed to discover effective therapeutic agents for AAA and identify potential natural compounds with pharmacological efficacy against the disease by targeting matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP2), a key enzyme involved in extracellular matrix degradation and aneurysm progression. METHODS: An integrated screening strategy combining cytotoxicity evaluation, high-content immunofluorescence imaging, and molecular docking was applied to an angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated rat aortic smooth muscle cells (RASMCs) model. A total of 138 natural products were systematically assessed. The anti-aneurysmal efficacy of the identified compound was further validated in both CaCl(2)-induced and Ang II-infused ApoE(-/-) mouse models of AAA. Network pharmacology and metabolomic analyses were performed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Salvianolic acid B (Sal B), a major polyphenol from Salvia miltiorrhiza, was identified as a potent anti‑AAA candidate. It suppressed aneurysm formation, reduced elastin degradation, and attenuated inflammatory infiltration in vivo, while preserving the contractile phenotype, lowering ROS, and inhibiting MMP activity in Ang II‑stimulated RASMCs in vitro. Mechanistically, Ang II suppresses NRF2, leading to downregulation of the System Xc(-)-GPX4 axis and promoting lipid peroxidation and VSMC ferroptosis. This ferroptosis then activates the AGE-RAGE pathway, amplifying inflammation and MMP‑driven matrix degradation. Sal B counteracts this cascade by restoring NRF2 activity, improving lipid metabolism, and inhibiting MMPs, thereby blocking ferroptosis‑initiated inflammation and preserving aortic integrity. CONCLUSION: Salvianolic acid B exerts protective effects against AAA by attenuating oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammation. These findings highlight Sal B as a promising natural therapeutic candidate for the prevention and treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract_zh: 背景：腹主动脉瘤（AAA）是一种危及生命的血管疾病，其特征为进行性主动脉壁退变、炎症和血管平滑肌细胞（VSMCs）丢失。尽管已有大量研究，目前仍无有效药物疗法可预防或阻止AAA进展。目的：本研究旨在通过靶向基质金属蛋白酶-2（MMP2）（一种参与细胞外基质降解和动脉瘤进展的关键酶），发现针对AAA的有效治疗药物，并识别具有药理学功效的潜在天然化合物。方法：采用整合筛选策略，结合细胞毒性评估、高内涵免疫荧光成像和分子对接，应用于血管紧张素II（Ang II）刺激的大鼠主动脉平滑肌细胞（RASMCs）模型。共系统评估了138种天然产物。所识别化合物的抗动脉瘤功效进一步在CaCl(2)诱导和Ang II输注的ApoE(-/-)小鼠AAA模型中验证。通过网络药理学和代谢组学分析阐明潜在分子机制。结果：丹酚酸B（Sal B），一种来自丹参的主要多酚，被鉴定为强效抗AAA候选物。它在体内抑制动脉瘤形成、减少弹性蛋白降解并减轻炎症浸润，同时在体外Ang II刺激的RASMCs中保持收缩表型、降低ROS并抑制MMP活性。机制上，Ang II抑制NRF2，导致System Xc(-)-GPX4轴下调，促进脂质过氧化和VSMC铁死亡。这种铁死亡随后激活AGE-RAGE通路，放大炎症和MMP驱动的基质降解。Sal B通过恢复NRF2活性、改善脂质代谢和抑制MMPs来对抗这一级联反应，从而阻断铁死亡引发的炎症并保持主动脉完整性。结论：丹酚酸B通过减轻氧化应激、铁死亡和炎症，对AAA发挥保护作用。这些发现凸显Sal B作为预防和治疗腹主动脉瘤的有前景的天然治疗候选物。
